surviving_claim: The file is not retracted and no measurement in it fails. Its 1 digest occurrence(s) name the panel the run was executed against, which is a true historical fact and the reason the run is comparable to the other arms. What is void is reading them as the current panel: ee1362df3f09 is a new freeze, so these fields no longer identify the panel in the tree. Nothing here recomputes quality against a rewritten cell -- the use phase this export records either produced no use records (measured: use_records is empty) or targets development cells only, so the nine regenerated cells are not reachable from this file.
note: artifact_sha256 is the git blob digest, so the marker is bound to the committed bytes rather than to one host line-ending policy. On a core.autocrlf checkout sha256_file sees CRLF and reports this marker stale; that is the checkout, not the artifact, and it is fixed by scoping the evidence trees in .gitattributes. Re-stamping freeze_digest to ee1362df3f09 is not a repair: it makes the checker pass by asserting that a quality verdict obtained against a regenerated cell is current.
